title: Gluten-Free Carrot Cake Cupcakes
shortDescription: Moist gluten-free carrot cupcakes with cream cheese swirl, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes use finely grated carrot to keep the crumb soft without any gluten in sight. I tested three gluten-free flour blends before landing on one that bakes tender, not gritty. A swirl of cream cheese frosting goes right on top, so you skip the piping bag if you want. The batter comes together in one bowl, no mixer required. Warm spices like cinnamon and nutmeg back up the carrot without taking over. This is a good pick for a gluten-free friend at a birthday party or a weekend baking project with kids.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups gluten-free all-purpose flour blend (with xanthan gum)
1 1/2 cups finely grated carrot (about 3 medium carrots)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
In a medium bowl, whisk gluten-free flour, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, granulated sugar, brown sugar, oil, and vanilla until smooth.
Fold the dry mix into the wet mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Stir in grated carrot and walnuts if using, until evenly spread through the batter.
Divide batter among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For frosting, beat cream cheese and butter together until smooth and light.
Add powdered sugar and vanilla, beat until fluffy. Chill 10 minutes if the frosting feels too soft to pipe.
Swirl frosting on fully cooled cupcakes with a piping bag or the back of a spoon.
tips: Grate carrot on the fine side of a box grater. Large shreds add too much moisture and can make the crumb gummy.
Squeeze grated carrot lightly in a paper towel if it looks very wet, especially with large carrots.
Check your gluten-free flour blend label. Blends without xanthan gum need 1/4 tsp added per cup of flour.
Chill frosted cupcakes 15 minutes before serving so the swirl holds its shape in warm rooms.

faq.question: Can I use pre-shredded carrots from a bag?
faq.answer: Pre-shredded carrots are cut too thick and dry out the batter. Grate fresh carrots on the fine side of a box grater for the best texture.

faq.question: Why did my gluten-free carrot cupcakes turn out dense?
faq.answer: Dense cupcakes usually mean overmixed batter or too much liquid from wet carrots. Mix just until combined and blot very wet carrot shreds first.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy-free too?
faq.answer: Swap the cream cheese and butter for dairy-free versions and check your oil is neutral. The cupcake base itself has no dairy in it already.

faq.question: How far ahead can I bake these cupcakes?
faq.answer: Bake cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Frost the same day you plan to serve them.

conclusion: These cupcakes prove gluten-free baking can still be moist and simple. Grated carrot and a quick cream cheese swirl make this one a repeat request in my house.
